title: HW 07
subtitle: Ch. 3 — Waves, Energy & the Bohr Model

questions.q: Match each comparison to the correct answer (not all terms are used).
items: A wave with frequency 1.0×10⁻⁹ Hz — is it high or low frequency vs. a wave at 1.0×10⁵ Hz?
Compared to radio waves, are x-rays high or low energy?
Compared to radio waves, are x-rays high or low frequency?
Compared to radio waves, are x-rays short or long wavelength?

questions.q: Select the correct statements below.
opts: Gamma ray energy is higher energy than visible light.
Gamma ray energy is higher frequency than visible light.
Gamma ray energy has a longer wavelength than visible light.
questions.note: Gamma rays have shorter wavelength than visible light, not longer — higher energy and frequency always mean shorter wavelength.

questions.q: Light was measured to have a frequency of 5.73×10¹⁵ Hz. What is the wavelength of the light (in m)?
Light was measured to have a wavelength of 3.9×10¹¹ m. What is the frequency of the light (in Hz)?
What is the wavelength (in nm) of infrared radiation that has a frequency of 9.76×10¹³ s⁻¹? (1 m = 10⁹ nm, c = 3.00×10⁸ m/s)
If the frequency is observed to be 1.00×10¹² Hz for a signal from electromagnetic radiation, what is the wavelength in cm? (c = 3.00×10⁸ m/s)
(Bonus) Light was measured to have a wavelength of 9.51×10² nm. What is the frequency of the light (in Hz)?
questions.given: λν = c  ·  c = 3.00×10⁸ m/s  ·  1 m = 10⁹ nm

questions.q: A radio wave has a frequency of 8.6×10⁸ Hz. What is the energy of one photon of this radiation? (h = 6.626×10⁻³⁴ J·s)
The frequency of a radio wave was measured to be 2.5×10⁸ Hz. What is the energy of the radio wave in kilojoules (kJ)?
questions.given: E = hν  ·  h = 6.626×10⁻³⁴ J·s  ·  watch the unit — answer in kJ, not J

questions.q: The frequency of a radio wave was measured to be 7.7×10⁸ Hz. What is the energy of the radio wave in kilojoules (kJ)?
questions.given: E = hν  ·  h = 6.626×10⁻³⁴ J·s  ·  watch the unit — answer in kJ, not J

questions.q: A photon has an energy of 4.21×10⁻¹⁵ J. What is its frequency? (h = 6.626×10⁻³⁴ J·s)
The energy of a wave is 3.95×10⁻²⁵ J. What is the frequency, measured in Hz?
Light was measured to have a wavelength of 7.51×10⁻⁹ m. What is the energy (in J) of that light wave?
questions.given: E = hc/λ  ·  c = 3.00×10⁸ m/s  ·  h = 6.626×10⁻³⁴ J·s

questions.q: What is the constant c (speed of light) used throughout the λν = c and E = hc/λ equations, in m/s?
The Bohr model of the atom describes the locations of the electrons as being in orbit-like paths around the nucleus.
Atomic orbitals developed using quantum mechanics describe probabilities of finding the electron, as opposed to exact paths for electrons.
If a sample of atoms is heated, it will emit a discrete, or line, spectrum.
A rainbow is an example of a continuous spectrum.
Which transition of a single electron in a 1-electron system would have the lowest energy?
questions.note: Energy levels get closer together as n increases, so the smallest gap — and lowest energy — is 6→3.

questions.q: Which transition of a single electron in a 1-electron system would have the lowest energy?
questions.note: Adjacent levels have the smallest energy gap.

questions.q: Which of the following electronic transitions of hydrogen has the highest (largest) frequency and thus releases the largest amount of energy?
questions.note: The largest jump between energy levels releases the most energy.

questions.q: Which of the following electronic transitions of hydrogen has the longest wavelength?
questions.note: Longest wavelength = lowest energy = smallest gap between levels (1→4 is an absorption with a large gap).

questions.q: Which of the following electronic transitions of hydrogen releases the longest wavelength emission?
questions.note: Among these emissions, 5→4 has the smallest energy gap and therefore the longest wavelength.

questions.note: A filled s² subshell has both electrons paired — 0 unpaired, never 1.
